statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-72897 ("Out-of-Bounds Access After SSL_set_SSL_CTX() During a Handshake") affects OpenSSL 3.4, 3.5, 3.6 and 4.0 and is fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.9: https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260929.txt, fix on the openssl-3.5 branch https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/4135f553c9d3ba4a09fe752f5d30af2a6a092b2e (ssl/ssl_lib.c). Debian fixed it for trixie in 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 (DSA-6531-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-72897). The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are built from Debian's trixie openssl source; the Debian changelog shipped in each package shows which Debian release it is built from. The builds of Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 and 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, including their FIPS builds in the DHI security repository, predate the fix. The first published rebuild of 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, the version used as the fixed boundary here, and every later build (the other three builds of 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and its FIPS build) carry Debian's 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 entry for this CVE in the libssl3t64 changelog, and in each of them, on amd64 and arm64, SSL_set_SSL_CTX in libssl.so.3 is larger than in the 3.5.7-1~deb13u2 builds (by 192 bytes on amd64 and 176 bytes on arm64) while neighbouring functions are unchanged, matching the fix. The FIPS builds ship the same libssl and libcrypto as the other builds of their Debian version, so they follow the same boundary. The FIPS provider module (fips.so, in the openssl-provider-fips packages) does not contain the affected TLS code, and the advisory states that no FIPS module is affected.
